#### `E2E-PERSISTENCE-02` — in-flight upload is not interrupted by in-app navigation

**Verdict:** FAIL

**Bullets:**
- ✗ panel shows an `uploading` entry whose progress percent is strictly between 0 and 100 | expected in-flight upload item before backend completion · observed no `[data-notif-status="uploading"]` in 20 samples at 100ms intervals
  → root cause: `NotificationPanel` owns a private `NotificationFeedModel` and no code wires `UploadPanel`'s local upload queue into that model; the panel only picked up the new video after the backend returned it in the server feed as `validating`.
- ✓ panel remains rendered during navigation | expected fixed panel · observed panel stayed rendered
- ✗ uploading entry remains across both navigations | expected stable in-flight entry · observed no uploading entry; after backend acceptance the panel showed `upload-sample` as server status `validating`
  → root cause: upload queue state is local to `UploadPanel`, not shared with the notification panel.
- ✓ upload completes successfully and creates DB row | expected new row for `upload-sample.mp4` with status `validating` · observed DB row exists
- ✗ new video appears in F04 library list after upload completes | expected library list/card update · observed page still showed `All videos 7` and the library body did not include `upload-sample`; only the notification panel showed it
  → root cause: unable to determine from browser evidence; upload completed in DB, but the rendered library list did not refresh during the observed flow.

## Soft-fails / Out-of-band

- `Detached HEAD DB collision avoided` — initial `HEAD` branch resolved to shared DB `videomax_head`; another process advanced seeded pipeline rows. Evaluator switched to branch `codex/evaluate-f11` so `init.sh` produced isolated DB `videomax_codex_evaluate_f11`.
- `Evaluator DB marker not available through project init script` — the project requires `./scripts/init.sh`; the run used the project-supported branch-derived DB instead of a literal `eval_f11_*` database.
- `Teardown` — `./scripts/stop.sh --clean` stopped dev processes and dropped `videomax_codex_evaluate_f11`; generated storage files from seeding/upload were removed after evidence capture.
